subject.title: [improvement] Sub-agent cascade circuit breaker for multi-agent team reliability

question: Should OpenClaw add a native persisted subagent spawn circuit breaker, and if so what scope, default enablement, failure taxonomy, cooldown/half-open, notification, and override behavior should become the supported product contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent behavior crosses config schema, persisted state, runtime spawn policy, UI/CLI surfacing, and overlapping provider/session/tool breakers, so automation should not choose the product contract.

options.title: Approve a bounded native breaker design
options.body: Add a generic subagent-runtime breaker with conservative defaults, SQLite-backed receipts, explicit failure classes, half-open or cooldown semantics, structured parent errors, and status/reset/override surfaces.

options.title: Fold this into a broader health breaker
options.body: Keep this issue open but make the canonical design live in the gateway/session/provider health-breaker work so subagents reuse the same failure taxonomy and operator controls.

options.title: Decline native breaker for now
options.body: Close or defer the request and keep relying on provider cooldowns, tool-loop detection, subagent timeouts, and custom operator hooks for cascade control.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded native breaker design
recommendation.body: Add a generic subagent-runtime breaker with conservative defaults, SQLite-backed receipts, explicit failure classes, half-open or cooldown semantics, structured parent errors, and status/reset/override surfaces.
